mainTopic: A husband's duty to ransom (פדיון) his captive wife: when she is forbidden to him, when he vowed against her, after his death, and when the ransom is very high.
overview: This amud finishes אביי's ruling that a husband married to a ממזרת or נתינה does not have to ransom her, since she can never come back to him as his wife. רבא gives a different test: if the captivity is what forbids her, he must ransom her, but if something else forbids her, he need not. The גמרא asks whether this matches a ברייתא where רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue about a husband who vowed against his wife and then she was captured. סומכוס explains that רבי יהושע's exemption applies only when the vow came before the capture, so husbands cannot use a vow as a trick. The גמרא tries to say the ברייתא is about the wife's own vow, but rejects that reading with two challenges. In the end, אביי and רבא each explain the ברייתא according to their own views. The amud then teaches that orphans do not have to ransom their father's widow, even if she was captured during his life. It then begins a ברייתא about paying a very high ransom: the husband must pay it the first time she is captured. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view continues on the next amud.

steps.title: No duty to ransom a ממזרת or נתינה married to a ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The ruling that began before this section ends here: a husband married to a ממזרת or נתינה does not have to ransom her, because she cannot return to him as his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ממזרת or a נתינה married to a ישראל: he does not have to ransom her, because I cannot apply to her the promise 'and I will bring you back to me as a wife.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of אביי's list, which began just before this point, of wives who are forbidden to their husbands. Here he rules that a ממזרת or נתינה married to a ישראל does not have to be ransomed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כתובה contains a promise: if she is captured, 'I will ransom you and bring you back to me as a wife.' A ממזרת or נתינה is forbidden to a ישראל anyway, so the 'bring you back as a wife' part can never happen. Since that part of the promise can't apply, he has no duty to ransom her.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman born from a forbidden relationship. She is forbidden to marry a regular ישראל.
A woman descended from the גבעונים. She is forbidden to marry a regular ישראל.
To ransom her, meaning to buy her freedom from captivity.
'And I will bring you back to me as a wife.' This is a promise written in the כתובה.

steps.confusionAlert: She still has a כתובה. The ruling only removes his duty to ransom her, because he cannot take her back as a wife.

phrases.english: A mamzeret or a Gibeonite woman married to an Israelite —
he is not obligated to redeem her,
since I do not apply to her
'And I will restore you to me as a wife.'
phrases.notes: These are words from the כתובה itself, the husband's written promises to his wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאֵין אֲנִי קוֹרֵא בָּהּ ״וְאוֹתְבִינִּךְ לִי לְאִנְתּוּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends a ruling that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a wife is forbidden to her husband anyway, as a ממזרת or נתינה is to a ישראל, he has no duty to ransom her, because the promise to take her back as a wife cannot apply.

steps.title: רבא's general rule: what is the cause of the prohibition?
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the test is the cause of her being forbidden. If the captivity forbids her, he must ransom her. If something else forbids her, he need not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: whenever the prohibition caused by her captivity is what forbids her, he must ransom her. When some other prohibition forbids her, he does not have to ransom her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own general rule for when a husband must ransom a wife who will be forbidden to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For example, a כהן's wife who is captured becomes forbidden to him only because of the captivity, so he must still ransom her. But if she was already forbidden for another reason, such as a widow married to a כהן גדול, he does not have to ransom her. רבא's test looks at what caused the prohibition, not only at whether she is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition caused by captivity. A captive woman becomes forbidden to a כהן.
Causes it for her. Here it means the reason she is forbidden.
A prohibition coming from something else, not from the captivity.

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule sets up the next question: is a wife forbidden by her husband's vow a case of 'something else'?

phrases.english: Rava said:
Any case where the prohibition of captivity causes it for her —
phrases.notes: He means the captivity itself is what makes her forbidden to her husband, like a כהן's wife who was captured.

phrases.english: he is obligated to redeem her,
where a prohibition of something else causes it for her —
he is not obligated to redeem her.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: כֹּל שֶׁאִיסּוּר שְׁבִיָּיה גּוֹרֵם לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with אביי's list in step 1 and offers a different, general test for when a forbidden wife must be ransomed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He must ransom her if the captivity is what forbids her. He need not ransom her if another prohibition forbids her.

steps.title: Is this a dispute between תנאים? A husband who vowed and then his wife was captured
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the disagreement about ransoming may match a ברייתא where רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue about a husband who vowed against his wife before she was captured.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this matches a dispute between תנאים? If a man vows that his wife may not benefit from him, and then she is captured: רבי אליעזר says he ransoms her and gives her the כתובה. רבי יהושע says he gives her the כתובה but does not ransom her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to show that the disagreement between the אמוראים is really an older dispute between תנאים, and it brings a ברייתא to compare.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband who vows that his wife may not benefit from him must divorce her, so she is forbidden to him because of the vow, not because of the captivity. רבי אליעזר still requires him to ransom her. רבי יהושע exempts him and requires only the כתובה payment. The question is whether these two views line up with the two views on ransoming a forbidden wife.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Shall we say it is like the תנאים?' The גמרא asks whether a disagreement matches an older dispute between תנאים.
A man who makes a vow that his wife may not benefit from him.
And she was taken captive.
Her כתובה, the money owed to her when the marriage ends.

steps.confusionAlert: Both תנאים agree that she gets her כתובה. They only disagree about whether he must also ransom her.

phrases.english: Let us say it is like a dispute of tanna'im:
One who vows against his wife, and she was taken captive —
Rabbi Eliezer says:
He redeems her, and gives her her marriage contract.
Rabbi Yehoshua says:
He gives her her marriage contract, and does not redeem her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to connect the disagreement on ransoming to a dispute between תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: The disagreement about whether a husband must ransom a wife who is forbidden to him for a reason other than captivity.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue about a husband who vowed against his wife and she was then captured.

steps.title: רבי נתן asks: did the vow come before or after the capture?
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן asked סומכוס whether רבי יהושע's ruling was about a vow made before the capture or after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן said: I asked סומכוס, when רבי יהושע said he gives her the כתובה and does not ransom her, did he mean that he vowed first and she was captured later, or that she was captured first and he vowed later?
steps.whatsHappening: Before going further, the ברייתא clarifies the case: רבי נתן wants to know the order of events in רבי יהושע's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the vow came first, the duty to ransom had not started yet when she became forbidden. If the capture came first, the duty to ransom had already started, and the vow would be cancelling it afterward. The order of events could change the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: I asked.
He made a vow forbidding her.
And afterward.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי נָתָן, שָׁאַלְתִּי אֶת סוֹמְכוֹס:
phrases.english: Rabbi Natan said: I asked Sumakhos:
When Rabbi Yehoshua said
he gives her her marriage contract and does not redeem her,
was it where he vowed against her and afterward she was captured,
or where she was captured and afterward he vowed against her?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי נָתָן, שָׁאַלְתִּי אֶת סוֹמְכוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the exact case of רבי יהושע's ruling from step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יהושע's exemption from ransom applies when the vow came before the capture, or after it.

steps.title: סומכוס: only when the vow came first, so the husband cannot use a trick
steps.stepSummary: סומכוס had no tradition on this, but he reasoned that רבי יהושע meant a vow made before the capture. Otherwise a husband could vow after the capture just to avoid paying the ransom.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: I did not hear a tradition, but it seems that it is where he vowed first and she was captured afterward. If you say it applies even when she was captured first and he vowed afterward, he would come to use trickery.
steps.whatsHappening: סומכוס answers רבי נתן's question using his own reasoning, since he had no tradition from his teachers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a vow made after the capture could release the husband, any husband could avoid an expensive ransom by vowing against his captive wife and paying only the כתובה. To block that trick, רבי יהושע's exemption must be limited to a vow made before the capture.

keyTerms.meaning: I did not hear, meaning I have no tradition from my teachers about this.
It seems, meaning it appears logical.
He will come to use trickery.

steps.whatToRemember: According to סומכוס, רבי יהושע exempts the husband from ransom only if the vow came before the capture. If a vow after the capture worked, husbands could use it as a trick to avoid ransoming their wives.

phrases.english: And he said to me: I have not heard,
but it would appear
that it is where he vowed against her and afterward she was captured.
For if you say
she was captured and afterward he vowed against her —
he will come to engage in trickery.
phrases.notes: He could make a vow against her right after she is captured, just to get out of paying the ransom.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר לִי: לֹא שָׁמַעְתִּי, וְנִרְאִין דְּבָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי נתן's question from step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהושע's exemption applies only when the vow came before the capture. Otherwise the husband could use a vow as a trick to avoid ransoming her.

steps.title: Matching אביי and רבא to the two תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the ברייתא is about a husband who vowed against his wife, a כהן's wife. On that reading, אביי holds like רבי אליעזר and רבא holds like רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it that they argue about a man who made a vow against his wife, a כהן's wife? Then אביי said his view like רבי אליעזר, and רבא said his view like רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the comparison it started in step 3. It suggests that the old argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע is the same as the argument between אביי and רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case she is forbidden to him because of his vow, not only because of the captivity. רבי אליעזר says he must ransom her, which fits אביי: he must ransom her even when something else forbids her. רבי יהושע says he does not have to ransom her, which fits רבא's test from step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: "What, is it not...?": the גמרא's way of offering a suggested reading
One who makes a vow that forbids someone (here, his wife) from getting benefit from him
The wife of a כהן
They argue about

phrases.english: What, is it not that
they argue about one who vows against his wife, a כהן's wife,
and אביי spoke like רבי אליעזר,
and רבא spoke like רבי יהושע?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לָאו: בְּמַדִּיר אֵשֶׁת כֹּהֵן קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the comparison begun in step 3, now that steps 4 and 5 have settled that the vow came before the capture.
steps.raayaObject: That the argument between אביי and רבא is an older argument between תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא in which רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue about a husband who vowed against his wife before she was captured.

steps.title: No, the ברייתא is about her vow that he left in place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the match. It says the ברייתא is about a wife who made the vow herself, and her husband let it stand. The two תנאים argue about whose fault that is.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. What case are we dealing with here? She made the vow, and he let it stand for her. רבי אליעזר holds: he is putting a finger between her teeth. רבי יהושע holds: she put a finger between her own teeth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion from step 6. It says the ברייתא is about a different case, so it has nothing to do with אביי and רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the question is not what caused her to be forbidden. The question is who is to blame for the vow. רבי אליעזר blames the husband, because he could have canceled her vow and did not. רבי יהושע blames the wife, because she is the one who said it.

keyTerms.meaning: "With what are we dealing here?": the גמרא is about to give the ברייתא a narrower case
He let her vow stand, by not canceling it when he heard it
"Puts a finger between her teeth": a picture of being the one who causes the harm

steps.confusionAlert: "Finger between her teeth" is a picture, not a real action. It just means "who is responsible for the vow staying in force."

phrases.english: No, with what are we dealing here?
Where she made the vow herself,
and he let it stand for her.
רבי אליעזר holds:
he is putting a finger between her teeth.
phrases.notes: He means the husband is to blame. So the husband must ransom her.

phrases.english: And רבי יהושע holds:
she put a finger between her own teeth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the match from step 6 by giving the ברייתא a different case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the תנאים argue about the same point as אביי and רבא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion assumed the husband made the vow. The ברייתא can be read as her vow that he let stand, so the argument is about blame.

steps.title: If it is her fault, why does she get her כתובה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer in step 7. If רבי יהושע blames the wife, why does he say the husband pays her כתובה?
steps.simpleTranslation: If she put a finger between her own teeth, what is the כתובה doing here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave in step 7. It points out that this reading does not fit רבי יהושע's own ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע rules that the husband gives her the כתובה but does not ransom her. If the vow is her fault, it makes sense that he does not ransom her. But then she should not get her כתובה either, so the reading in step 7 seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: The money a husband must pay his wife when the marriage ends
"What is its business here?": why should it apply?

phrases.aramaic: אִי הִיא נָתְנָה אֶצְבַּע בֵּין שִׁינֶּיהָ
phrases.english: If she put a finger between her own teeth,
what is the כתובה doing here?
phrases.notes: In the ברייתא, רבי יהושע says he gives her the כתובה. A wife who is to blame should not get it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הִיא נָתְנָה אֶצְבַּע בֵּין שִׁינֶּיהָ כְּתוּבָּה מַאי עֲבִידְתַּהּ
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that רבי יהושע blames the wife for her own vow.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the wife is to blame, she should lose her כתובה. But רבי יהושע says the husband pays it.

steps.title: A second challenge begins: the גמרא quotes רבי נתן's question again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a second challenge to step 7 by quoting רבי נתן's question to סומכוס again, together with סומכוס's reply. The challenge itself comes in the next step.
steps.simpleTranslation: And more: רבי נתן said, I asked סומכוס: when רבי יהושע said he gives her the כתובה but does not ransom her, was that when he vowed against her and then she was captured? Or when she was captured and then he vowed against her? He said: I did not hear a tradition about this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a second challenge to the answer in step 7 by repeating the ברייתא from step 4. The challenge itself comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quotation brings back סומכוס's before-or-after distinction and his reason for it from step 5: a husband could otherwise vow after the capture as a trick. The next step uses this to show that the reading in step 7, that she vowed, does not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: "And furthermore": a second challenge is coming
He made a vow against her
She was taken captive
Ransoms her

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא brings two challenges against reading the ברייתא as the wife's vow. First, she would not deserve the כתובה (step 8). Second, סומכוס's before-or-after distinction would make no sense (step 10).

phrases.english: And furthermore,
רבי נתן said,
phrases.notes: This is the same ברייתא from step 4. The גמרא quotes it again to make a new point.

phrases.english: I asked סומכוס:
When רבי יהושע said
he gives her the כתובה and does not ransom her,
was it when he vowed against her and afterward she was captured,
or when she was captured and afterward he vowed against her?
And he said: I did not hear a tradition about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ, אָמַר רַבִּי נָתָן, שָׁאַלְתִּי אֶת סוֹמְכוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge to the דחיה in step 7, on top of the one in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the ברייתא is about a vow the wife made.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: סומכוס's distinction between a vow before the capture and a vow after it depends on the worry that a husband might trick his way out of paying. The next step shows that this worry makes no sense if the wife made the vow.

steps.title: The second problem: if she vowed, timing should not matter
steps.stepSummary: If the wife made the vow herself, there is no reason to care whether the vow came before or after the capture.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if she is the one who vowed, what difference does it make whether he upheld her vow and later she was captured, or she was captured and later he upheld her vow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now delivers the second challenge it set up in step 9. If the wife made the vow, as step 7 says, the before-or-after distinction no longer makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סומכוס said the vow had to come before the capture, so a husband could not vow afterward just to get out of paying the ransom (step 5). That worry only makes sense if the husband made the vow. If she made it herself, there is no trick to guard against, so the timing should not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: She vowed (the wife made the vow herself)
What difference does it make to me? Shows that two cases should be the same
She was taken captive

phrases.english: And if it is where she herself vowed,
what difference is it to me if he upheld her vow and then she was captured,
phrases.notes: This is the before-capture case סומכוס spoke about in step 5.

phrases.english: or she was captured and then he upheld her vow?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second challenge (וְתוּ) against step 7, which began with the quote in step 9. It follows the first challenge in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 7's claim that the ברייתא is about the wife's own vow.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: סומכוס's before-or-after distinction only matters if the husband could vow to avoid paying. If the wife vowed, that worry disappears, so the distinction would be pointless.

steps.title: Back to the husband's vow: each אמורא explains it his own way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the wife's-vow reading. The husband vowed, and both אביי and רבא can explain the ברייתא according to their own views.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is really a case where he made her vow. And אביי explains it according to his reasoning, and רבא explains it according to his reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on step 7 and goes back to the reading that the husband made the vow. This line sets up the next steps, where it shows how אביי and רבא each explain the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said that if the husband vowed, אביי must hold like רבי אליעזר and רבא like רבי יהושע. Now the גמרא says that is not necessary. Each אמורא can fit the ברייתא into his own view, so neither has to be against a תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. Drops the earlier answer
Really, actually. Goes back to the original reading
He made her vow (the husband forbade her from benefiting from him)
He explains it according to his own reasoning

phrases.english: Rather, it is really where he made her vow.
And אביי explains it according to his reasoning,
and רבא explains it according to his reasoning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenges of steps 8 to 10, drops step 7, and goes back to the husband's-vow reading from step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each side explains the source according to his own view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Step 6 thought that if the husband vowed, אביי and רבא must each side with a different תנא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The husband did vow, but both אביי and רבא can explain the whole ברייתא within their own views.
steps.whyThisMatters: This removes the problem that one אמורא would be arguing against a תנא.

steps.title: אביי: the cases everyone agrees on
steps.stepSummary: According to אביי, everyone agrees that a widow married to a כהן גדול, and a כהן's wife whom he forbade by vow, must be ransomed. A ממזרת or נתינה married to an Israelite need not be.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי explains it his way: for a widow married to a כהן גדול, everyone agrees he must ransom her. For a ממזרת or נתינה married to an Israelite, everyone agrees he does not have to ransom her. A man who forbids by vow his wife, a כהן's wife, also must ransom her according to everyone, because that is the same as a widow married to a כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts אביי's explanation by listing the cases where רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע do not argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי follows his own earlier ruling: a widow married to a כהן גדול must be ransomed, but a ממזרת or נתינה married to an Israelite need not be. A כהן's wife who is captured is forbidden to him anyway, so the vow changes nothing. Her case is like the widow married to a כהן גדול, and he must ransom her.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow married to a כהן גדול, a marriage the תורה forbids
A ממזרת and a נתינה (Gibeonite woman), both forbidden to marry an Israelite
Everyone agrees; there is no dispute
He must ransom her from captivity
One who forbids his wife by a vow

phrases.english: אביי explains it according to his reasoning:
A widow married to a כהן גדול:

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּחַיָּיב לִפְדּוֹתָהּ,
phrases.english: everyone agrees that he must ransom her.
A ממזרת or a נתינה married to an Israelite:

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּאֵינוֹ חַיָּיב לִפְדּוֹתָהּ.
phrases.english: everyone agrees that he does not have to ransom her.
One who forbids by vow a כהן's wife, too:

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּחַיָּיב לִפְדּוֹתָהּ.
phrases.english: everyone agrees that he must ransom her,
since that is the same as a widow married to a כהן גדול.
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording; some versions don't have them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins carrying out the plan announced in step 11, starting with אביי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the dispute to certain cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Step 6 thought the תנאים argue in every vow case, so אביי must side with רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: A כהן's wife falls under the agreed rule, so she must be ransomed according to everyone.

steps.title: אביי: the dispute is only about an Israelite's wife
steps.stepSummary: According to אביי, the תנאים argue only when an Israelite forbids his wife by vow. רבי אליעזר looks at the start of the marriage, and רבי יהושע looks at the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they argue is when an Israelite forbids his wife by vow. רבי אליעזר goes by the beginning, and רבי יהושע goes by the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes אביי's explanation by showing the one case where the two תנאים really argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An Israelite could have taken his captive wife back, and only his vow stops him. רבי אליעזר looks at the time of the כתובה, when he took on the duty to ransom her, so the duty remains. רבי יהושע looks at the final situation: he cannot take her back, so he does not have to ransom her. Since אביי agrees about the כהן's wife, he does not contradict either תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: Where they do argue
Goes by, follows
At the beginning (when the כתובה was written)
At the end (the situation now)

steps.whatToRemember: For אביי, a כהן's wife must be ransomed according to everyone. The argument between רבי אליעזר (the beginning) and רבי יהושע (the end) is only about an Israelite's wife.

phrases.english: Where they argue is about one who forbids by vow an Israelite's wife.
רבי אליעזר goes by the beginning,
and רבי יהושע goes by the end.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes אביי's explanation by naming the case that is in dispute.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Places the dispute in a narrower case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Step 6 thought אביי could only agree with רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute is only about an Israelite's wife, which leaves room for אביי's own view according to both תנאים.

steps.title: רבא: the dispute covers every vow case
steps.stepSummary: According to רבא, everyone agrees that the forbidden-marriage cases do not need ransoming. The argument is about a vow, whether she is a כהן's wife or an Israelite's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא explains it his way: for a widow married to a כהן גדול, and a ממזרת or נתינה married to an Israelite, everyone agrees he does not have to ransom her. Where they argue is about one who forbids his wife by vow, whether she is a כהן's wife or an Israelite's wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now shows how רבא explains the ברייתא according to his own view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's own ruling is that in all the forbidden-marriage cases the husband need not ransom his wife, and he says everyone agrees about that. The vow cases are where the תנאים argue, both for a כהן's wife and for an Israelite's wife. Because the forbidden-marriage cases are kept out of the dispute, רבא does not contradict either תנא.

keyTerms.term: בֵּין אֵשֶׁת כֹּהֵן וּבֵין אֵשֶׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל
keyTerms.meaning: Both a כהן's wife and an Israelite's wife

steps.confusionAlert: אביי and רבא disagree about the widow married to a כהן גדול. For אביי he must ransom her; for רבא he does not. Each one says 'everyone agrees' about his own ruling.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא's final reading: the husband vowed. אביי says the תנאים argue only about an Israelite's wife. רבא says they argue about every vow case. Each fits the ברייתא into his own view.

phrases.english: רבא explains it according to his reasoning:
A widow married to a כהן גדול,
or a ממזרת or a נתינה married to an Israelite:

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּאֵינוֹ חַיָּיב לִפְדּוֹתָהּ.
phrases.english: everyone agrees that he does not have to ransom her.
Where they argue is about one who forbids his wife by vow,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין אֵשֶׁת כֹּהֵן וּבֵין אֵשֶׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: whether she is a כהן's wife or an Israelite's wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבא's version, parallel to אביי's explanation in steps 12 and 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the source according to his own view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Step 6 thought רבא could only agree with רבי יהושע.
steps.terutzMaskana: The forbidden-marriage cases are agreed by everyone, and the dispute is only about vows, so רבא fits with both תנאים.

steps.title: According to רבא: start of the marriage versus end
steps.stepSummary: Under רבא's reading, רבי אליעזר looks at the start of the marriage and רבי יהושע looks at the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר goes by how things were at the beginning, and רבי יהושע goes by how things are at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבא's explanation of the argument by giving the reason behind each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the argument is about a husband who forbade his wife to himself by a vow. רבי אליעזר says he must ransom her because she was permitted to him when he wrote the כתובה. רבי יהושע says he is exempt because now, at the end, he cannot take her back as his wife.

keyTerms.meaning: goes after, follows (decides based on)
at the beginning, at the outset
at the end

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same sentence the גמרא used for אביי in step 13. Here it is said again for רבא, whose case is different: a vow made by a כהן or by an Israelite.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer goes by the beginning,
phrases.notes: When the כתובה was written, she was still permitted to him, so his duty to ransom her started then.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehoshua goes by the end.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי אליעזר אזיל בתר מעיקרא ורבי יהושע אזיל בתר בסוף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's explanation from step 14 by giving each תנא's reasoning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the reasoning of both sides of the argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It was not yet clear why the two תנאים argue about a vow in רבא's view.
steps.terutzMaskana: They argue about whether we go by the time of the marriage or by the situation now.

steps.title: Heirs must ransom her if the husband knew she was captured
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that if she was captured during her husband's life and then he died, the heirs must ransom her only if he knew about the capture.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if she was captured, he must ransom her. The Rabbis taught: if she was captured while her husband was alive and then her husband died, and her husband knew about her capture, the heirs must ransom her. If her husband did not know, the heirs do not have to ransom her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the line of the משנה about ransoming a captive wife and brings a ברייתא about what happens when the husband dies before he can ransom her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new question is whether the husband's duty passes to his heirs. This ברייתא says it does, but only if the duty already took hold while he was alive, meaning he knew she was captured.

keyTerms.meaning: she was taken captive
to ransom her, to buy her freedom
he knew about her (that she was captured)
heirs

phrases.english: "If she was captured, he must ransom her," and so on.
The Rabbis taught:
If she was captured while her husband was alive,
and afterward her husband died:
if her husband knew about her capture,
the heirs must ransom her.
If her husband did not know about her capture,
the heirs do not have to ransom her.

steps.triggerLanguage: נשבית חייב לפדותה וכו׳ תנו רבנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the vow discussion ended: does the ransom duty pass to the heirs?
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the husband knew of the capture before he died, his heirs must ransom her. If he did not know, they need not.

steps.title: רב tells לוי the הלכה does not follow this ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: לוי wanted to rule according to the ברייתא, but רב told him that his uncle said the הלכה is not like it.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי planned to make a real ruling based on this ברייתא. רב said to him: this is what my uncle said: the הלכה is not like this ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story where the ברייתא from the last step is pushed aside for practical ruling. It is setting up the next step, which says which ברייתא we do follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is not shown to be wrong by an argument. Instead, רב passes on a tradition from his uncle, רבי חייא, that the practical הלכה does not follow it.

keyTerms.meaning: to make a practical ruling in a real case
a ברייתא, a teaching from the time of the משנה
my uncle (רב's name for רבי חייא)
the הלכה is not

phrases.english: Levi planned to make a real ruling
according to this ברייתא.
Rav said to him:
This is what my uncle said:
phrases.notes: "My uncle" is רבי חייא, רב's uncle.

phrases.english: The הלכה is not like this ברייתא,

steps.triggerLanguage: לוי סבר למיעבד עובדא כי הא מתניתא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the ruling of the ברייתא in step 16 as the practical הלכה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the ברייתא of step 16 for practical ruling.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A tradition from רבי חייא says the הלכה does not follow it.

steps.title: Orphans never have to ransom their father's widow
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה follows a different ברייתא: orphans do not ransom her, even if she was captured while her husband was alive, because she can no longer go back to being his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the הלכה is like what another ברייתא teaches: if she was captured after her husband died, the orphans do not have to ransom her. And more than that: even if she was captured while her husband was alive and then he died, the orphans do not have to ransom her, because I cannot apply to her the promise "I will take you back as my wife."
steps.whatsHappening: רב finishes his statement by bringing the ברייתא that the הלכה does follow, which says the heirs are always exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband's duty to ransom comes from his promise in the כתובה to take her back as his wife. Once he has died, that promise cannot be kept, so the duty ends. It makes no difference whether he knew about the capture.

keyTerms.meaning: orphans (the husband's children, his heirs)
and not only that, but even
"and I will take you back as my wife" (a line in the כתובה)

steps.whatToRemember: The duty to ransom a wife is tied to bringing her back as a wife. After the husband dies, that is impossible, so his heirs do not have to ransom her, even if he knew she was captured.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two ברייתות. The first says the heirs must ransom her if the husband knew. The second, which is the הלכה, says they never have to.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the reason behind the whole ransom duty: it comes from the promise to restore the marriage, not from a general debt the husband owes.

phrases.english: rather, it is like what is taught in this ברייתא:
If she was captured after her husband's death,
the orphans do not have to ransom her.
And not only that, but
even if she was captured while her husband was alive,
and afterward her husband died,
the orphans do not have to ransom her,
because I cannot apply to her
"and I will take you back as my wife."
phrases.notes: These are the words of the husband's promise in the כתובה. A dead husband can no longer keep it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב's statement from step 17 by naming the ברייתא that the הלכה follows.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Orphans never have to ransom their father's widow, because the promise to take her back as a wife can no longer be kept.

steps.title: A very high ransom: he must pay the first time only
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that if the captors ask up to ten times her value, the husband must pay the first time. After that he may choose. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is about to give another view.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: if she was captured and they asked him for up to ten times her value, the first time he must ransom her. From then on, if he wants he ransoms her, and if he wants he does not. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about how much the husband must pay and how many times. The last line starts רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view, which continues in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally captives are not ransomed for more than their value. Here the husband must pay even ten times her value, but only the first time she is captured. After that, ransoming her again is his own choice.

keyTerms.meaning: her value, the normal ransom price for her
the first time
from here on, after that
if he wants

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If she was captured and they were asking him for
up to ten times her value,
the first time, he ransoms her.
From then on:
if he wants, he ransoms her;
if he wants, he does not ransom her.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

steps.triggerLanguage: תנו רבנן נשבית והיו מבקשין ממנו עד עשרה בדמיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about the ransom duty: how much he must pay and how many times.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband must pay a ransom of up to ten times her value the first time she is captured. After that it is his choice.
